questions.question: What is the most common location for a "splenule" (accessory spleen)?
questions.detail: Splenules are commonly found in the splenic hilum and the pancreatic tail, where their presence can sometimes mimic other masses.

questions.question: Which nuclear medicine scan can be used to confirm that a mass is a splenule?
choices: B. Tc-99m sulfur colloid or heat-damaged RBC scan
questions.detail: Functioning splenic tissue can be identified using Tc-99m sulfur colloid or heat-damaged RBC scans.

questions.question: "Gamna-Gandy bodies" (siderotic nodules) demonstrate "blooming" (increased darkness) on which MRI sequence?
questions.detail: Siderotic nodules contain iron, which causes magnetic dephasing that becomes more pronounced (blooms) with longer echo times (TE) on in-phase GRE sequences.

questions.question: When evaluating a cystic splenic lesion on ultrasound, what must always be used to exclude a vascular etiology (like an aneurysm)?
questions.detail: Color Doppler is essential to rule out splenic artery aneurysms, which can sonographically mimic simple cysts.

questions.question: Which of the following is a "hypervascular" splenic lesion?
questions.detail: While infarcts, abscesses, and lymphomas are generally hypovascular, splenic hemangiomas are considered hypervascular lesions.

questions.question: Splenic "infarcts" characteristically appear on CT as:
choices: B. Peripheral wedge-shaped regions of non-enhancement
questions.detail: Infarcts typically present as peripheral, wedge-shaped areas that do not enhance, following the segmental blood supply of the spleen.

questions.question: "Splenosis" refers to:
choices: B. Autotransplantation of splenic tissue after trauma/surgery
C. Iron overload in the spleen
E. Congenital absence of the spleen
questions.detail: Splenosis occurs when traumatic rupture of the spleen allows splenic cells to seed the peritoneum and develop into functional nodules.

questions.question: An enlarged spleen measuring >13 cm in craniocaudal dimension is a secondary sign of:
questions.detail: Splenomegaly, defined as a craniocaudal dimension greater than 13 cm, is often a result of chronic passive congestion caused by portal hypertension.
